title: Which block on the calendar adds to thirty six?
description: A two by two block on a calendar page has the sum thirty six. The block is written with the letter eigh, the sum is made into an equation, and the dates are found and checked. Keeko doubts that the block starts at nine.
teaching_notes: One idea: in a two by two block, the date to the right is one more and the date below is seven more, so the four dates add to four eigh plus sixteen. Watch for students who share the sum equally among the four dates.

source: A friend picks a 2 by 2 block from a calendar page and says the sum is 36
video_script.why: A child writes the four dates of a calendar block with one letter, forms an equation from their sum, and finds the block.
video_script.substitution: a two by two block on a calendar page, with the sum thirty six and the letter eigh for the first date
video_script.anchor: a calendar page with a two by two block shaded and the words the sum is 36
video_script.wrong_move: shares the sum equally among the four dates, forgetting that the dates are not equal
video_script.payoff_line: The block is five, six, twelve and thirteen.

final_answer.spoken: the block is five, six, twelve and thirteen

maths_rules: Block a, a + 1, a + 7, a + 8; the sum is 4a + 16.
Another block 6, 7, 13, 14 adds to 40, and 4 x 6 + 16 = 40.
Doubt: 36 / 4 = 9 gives 9, 10, 16, 17 which add to 52, not 36.
video_script.design: One idea: write the four dates with one letter and solve for it. The calendar page stays in the anchor band and the equation sits on the working board.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This question is from your book. A friend picks a two by two block from a calendar page.
<bookmark mark='cal'/>The block has four dates, and the friend says their sum is thirty six.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which four dates are in the block?

beats.on_screen: the calendar page holds still and the shaded block glows

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a calendar strip: the date 8 has 9 on its right and 15 below it; arrows show plus 1 across and plus 7 down

marks.across: an arrow marked plus 1 runs from 8 to 9
marks.down: an arrow marked plus 7 runs from 8 to 15

narration: <bookmark mark='across'/>On a calendar, the date to the right is one more.
<bookmark mark='down'/>A week has seven days, so the date below is seven more.

beats.on_screen: Given: a two by two block of a calendar; the sum of its four dates is 36

marks.given: the block and the sum 36 are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a two by two block of a calendar. The sum of its four dates is thirty six.

beats.on_screen: To find: the four dates of the block

marks.find: the thing to find is written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the four dates.

beats.on_screen: block: a, a + 1 over a + 7, a + 8; sum = a + (a + 1) + (a + 7) + (a + 8) = 4a + 16

marks.block: a, a + 1, a + 7 and a + 8 are written in the block

narration: <bookmark mark='block'/>Step one, call the first date eigh. The date to its right is eigh plus one. Below them are eigh plus seven and eigh plus eight.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>The four dates add to four eigh plus sixteen.
<bookmark mark='eq'/>Step two, four eigh plus sixteen equals thirty six.
<bookmark mark='take'/>Take away sixteen, and four eigh is twenty.
<bookmark mark='five'/>Divide by four, and eigh is five.

marks.dates: 5, 6, 12 and 13 are written in the block

narration: <bookmark mark='dates'/>Step three, with eigh equal to five, the dates are five, six, twelve and thirteen.
<bookmark mark='check'/>Check, five plus six plus twelve plus thirteen is thirty six.

marks.sum: 6 + 7 + 13 + 14 = 40 and 4 x 6 + 16 = 40 are written and ticked

narration: <bookmark mark='other'/>Step four, try the rule on another block. It starts at six, so its dates are six, seven, thirteen and fourteen.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>They add to forty, and four times six plus sixteen is also forty.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The block is five, six, twelve and thirteen.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand; Keeko's bubble shows 36 / 4 = 9; the block 9, 10, 16, 17 is shaded on the calendar and 52 is written beside 36; the bubble is struck out

marks.test: the block 9, 10, 16, 17 is shaded and its sum 52 is written beside 36

narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.
<bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the block starts at nine, because thirty six shared by four is nine.
<bookmark mark='test'/>Test it. The dates nine, ten, sixteen and seventeen add to fifty two.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>That is not thirty six. The four dates are not equal, so the sum cannot be shared evenly.
